headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection/data-flow exposure from pipecat’s shared bus and API-backed outputs; python-cheatsheet is read-only and non-networked, limiting blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pipecat explicitly uses a shared bus and can ingest/emit text, audio, and API-backed model outputs; if python-cheatsheet content is bridged into that bus, it could be treated as instructions. python-cheatsheet itself is documentation-only and non-interactive, so it is not an active injector, but the pair still has a plausible default pathway via shared state.
conditions: IF pipecat consumes content from the shared bus as trusted instructions, injection is possible.
IF python-cheatsheet text is manually copied into pipecat prompts, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Separate the shared bus into per-session channels.
Prefix all imported text with untrusted-data markers.
Add a prompt firewall that strips instruction-like patterns.
Review any copied cheat-sheet text before pasting.
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tags on bus messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: pipecat touches audio, video, images, text, and conversation state and can send data to allowlisted external APIs; python-cheatsheet touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network access. The pair does not show a shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage is limited to pipecat’s outbound integrations rather than cross-agent exfiltration.
conditions: IF pipecat is configured with external STT/LLM/TTS providers, conversation content may leave the local environment.
IF sensitive audio or text is routed through pipecat, those contents can appear in third-party inference logs.
mitigations: Disable external providers in pipecat where possible.
Route only non-sensitive test data through the pair.
Confirm allowlisted endpoints before deployment.
Minimize conversation-state retention in pipecat.
requires-engineering: add per-field redaction before outbound calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: pipecat has shared-bus concurrency and multiple instances; python-cheatsheet has no write, shell, or network capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is unlikely. Uncertainty is low because B is read-only and A’s writes are not exposed here.
conditions: IF pipecat instances are pointed at the same external mutable backend, write contention could occur.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same writable directory, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid sharing mutable backends between instances.
Serialize any writes through one coordinator.
Check that python-cheatsheet remains read-only.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: pipecat can generate speech/text from upstream model calls, and python-cheatsheet is a reference source that could be treated as authoritative content. If pipecat output is fed into a writing workflow without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect prose or actions. python-cheatsheet does not verify outputs, so the pair lacks a built-in correction step.
conditions: IF pipecat-generated text is reused by the writing agent without human review, errors can propagate.
IF the cheatsheet content is used as ground truth for downstream decisions, mistaken facts can cascade.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before reuse.
Require citations for any factual claims.
Compare outputs against a second source.
Keep python-cheatsheet as reference-only.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, and neither profile shows regulated-data handling, residency constraints, or special certifications. The main compliance concern is pipecat’s outbound API use on potentially sensitive audio/text, while python-cheatsheet has no data handling. Because only A has relevant compliance exposure, B is not cited beyond its lack of data classes.
conditions: IF regulated audio or text is processed through pipecat, external provider terms may apply.
IF deployment requires strict residency, allowlisted third-party endpoints may be noncompliant.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in pipecat.
Verify provider DPAs and residency settings.
Document which endpoints receive content.
Keep python-cheatsheet outside regulated workflows.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing.
